findings.description: The new flag-presence rule (comment: 'a flag's presence, never its value, decides') is enforced for --record-fallback (empty value is a usage error) and for --reason without --record-fallback, but not for --since. `--since) fallback_since="${2:-}"; _since_given=1; ...` followed by `_adv_record_fallback ... "$fallback_since"` means `--record-fallback failed --since ""` (or `--since` as the last argument) is accepted and passed through as 'no --since'. The --since guard is what refuses to displace an envelope newer than the aborted run's start (CMP-146); a skill that composes the command from a captured start timestamp that came back empty loses that guard silently and the failed record displaces whatever envelope stands, including a later retry's completed one.
findings.failure_mode: An automated caller passes an empty --since value; the fallback record is written without the newer-envelope refusal and overwrites a completed envelope with a failed record (moved to .prev, not restored).
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the --record-fallback check: `if [[ -n "$_since_given" && -z "$fallback_since" ]]; then error "--since needs a timestamp"; exit 2; fi` before the `_adv_record_fallback` call, so an empty value is a usage error rather than a dropped guard.

findings.description: In the --diff-range block main registers `trap 'command rm -f -- "$_ADV_RANGE_DIFF"' EXIT`. A few lines later, after the workdir is created, main registers `trap '_adv_cleanup_on_exit' EXIT`, which replaces (not chains) the earlier EXIT trap. From that point the range-diff temp file under TMPDIR is removed only if `_adv_cleanup_on_exit` (outside this diff) knows about `_ADV_RANGE_DIFF`. The diff itself gives no evidence that it does; if it does not, every --diff-range run leaves a copy of the reviewed diff in TMPDIR.
findings.failure_mode: Each --diff-range run (the skills' default path since the audit's git-diff grant was replaced) leaks a `adversarial-range-XXXXXX` file containing the full reviewed diff in a shared TMPDIR.
findings.suggested_fix: Either have `_adv_cleanup_on_exit` remove `${_ADV_RANGE_DIFF:-}` (guarded with `|| true`), or move the range file into the run workdir once it exists, so the single cleanup trap covers it. Add a test asserting no `adversarial-range-*` file survives a --diff-range run.

findings.description: The synthetic 'every hop of the primary chain was ceded to the companion' envelope hardcodes `status: "api_failure", degraded: false` for both gates. process_findings sets `degraded: true` for an audit API failure (the nineteenth-run refutation of a3 C-003 states this rule). When the subsequent fold fails (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`), the audit envelope written to disk says `api_failure` with `degraded: false`, which the audit gate's DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW rule and verdict-derive read differently from a process_findings-produced api_failure envelope.
findings.failure_mode: An audit run whose primary chain was entirely ceded and whose fold then failed writes an api_failure envelope with degraded:false, inconsistent with every other audit api_failure envelope and with the audit resource's degraded rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `degraded` from the gate in the synthetic: `--argjson degraded "$([[ "$type" == audit ]] && echo true || echo false)"`, matching process_findings' api_failure shape; or route the synthetic through the same helper process_findings uses to build its failure envelope.
